notation: Logical Arabic in the English's notation (engines.sf2_arabic): its tags pass to the game as they are ({N} a new line, {W1} and {W2} a wait for the button, {D1} to {D3} a pause, {CLEAR} the window cleared, {NAME;0} the name the player gave, {LEADER}, {NAME}, {ITEM}, {SPELL}, {CLASS} and {#} what the game writes). The encoder breaks the lines itself, 212 pixels a line, and {N} breaks one where it stands; the window shows two lines (three in the witch's scene) and scrolls on. A name counts 70 pixels, an item, a spell or a class 96, a number 40. A string holds Arabic letters, spaces, Western or Arabic-Indic digits and the punctuation . , : ! - … ، ؛ ؟ only. No vowel marks: the font has none.

entries.context: A new game: a witch in a forest greets the player with a cackle; the player has come at last (the window is cleared first, and waits)
The witch: the player looks confused, and does not know why they are there
entries.text: آه، تبدو حائرا جدا.{N}ألا تعرف لماذا أنت هنا؟{W2}

entries.context: The witch repeats the name the player has just given ({NAME;0}), and likes it
